limits: No trajectory parity with the original is claimed: drivers, physics and scheduling are native, and a field amplifies the recorded native/reference difference. Scheduling, structure and repeatability are what is compared.
BT drivers still have no opponent handling; the inflated first-lap times are the evidence, and they must not be presented as a traffic AI.
The runtime runs every car's pit block before any car's timing, where the original interleaves them per car; nothing in the pit block feeds another car's timing.
Human input is sampled at the original 0.02 s robot interval, unlike the existing practice DrivingRuntime which applies input every physics tick.
Only one human entry is supported and the human car has no robot policy.
The driving window is not connected to this runtime: opponent selection, live standings and race results in the UI are later work.
Accumulated penalty time is not fed into pit service timing yet.
Qualifying does not feed a race grid; championships and replay remain unimplemented.
This driver never cuts past the original threshold on Aalborg, so its measured race penalty time is zero; the penalty arithmetic itself is compared against the original separately.
The diagnostic uses one car model and one setup per race, though the runtime accepts a different definition per entry.
priority: Gameplay; foliage and new graphical work deferred
scope: One runtime in original ReOneStep order: race clock, 0.02 s robot scheduling for BT and human entries, multi-car physics, per-car pit management, ReManage timing and gaps, complete ReRaceRules and ReSortCars, with race results

verification.gating: Release suite gated on the three-digit total line with no runtime-failure, Fatal, failed-case or signal markers
verification.oracleComparison: Robot callback cadence and prestart length compared against the G1 multi-car oracle over the same tick range
